slides.title: On Pim's counter
slides.text: On Pim's counter sit a postcard and a sealed envelope. Anyone can read the postcard, but the envelope keeps its words hidden.
slides.alt: The sealed route: a message travels a road marked sealed, the padlock idea played as a journey.

focus.cue: The open street: anyone on it can read the post, like a postcard
The padlock street is sealed, like an envelope

slides.title: Open like a postcard
slides.text: An open network is like a postcard. Anyone nearby could read what travels on it, so it is not a place for private things.
slides.alt: The sealed route: a message travels a road marked sealed, the padlock idea played as a journey.

focus.cue: Pim: the snoopy cat reads everything on the open street

slides.title: Spot the seal
slides.text: Before typing anything private, Pim looks for one small symbol. The padlock means this connection is sealed, like an envelope.
steps: no padlock: treat it as a postcard
padlock showing: the trip is sealed
not sure: stop and ask a trusted adult
slides.alt: Sealed roads wear padlocks: open roads cost one hop, but a snoopy cat reads every packet on them.

focus.cue: Open roads have a snoopy cat who reads packets

slides.title: What a seal cannot promise
slides.text: A sealed envelope proves the trip is private. It does not prove the sender is kind, so still think before you trust a message.
slides.alt: A second message card to judge: is it a trick with clues, or a safe message with none?

focus.cue: This message wears a bank's name
A seal on the trip says nothing about the sender

slides.title: The most open road
slides.text: Public networks in cafés and trains are the most open road of all. Save private things for your home network instead.

words.means: closed tight, so no one can peek inside on the trip
an open message that anyone carrying it can read
a small lock symbol that shows a connection is sealed
a shared network in a public place, open to many people

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Packet Post at Rules of the Road and play its 2 levels: say when each packet arrives, and resend the ones that go missing.
slides.alt: Say Got It begins: three packets are on the road to the mill office, and the second one has fallen off the van.

focus.cue: Play Rules of the Road: arrivals and resends
